title: The Cold Colony
premise: Petra Thackeray, a cargo hauler and former insurance investigator, intercepts a distress beacon broadcasting in Vessic—a language officially extinct since the Meridian Massacre two hundred years ago. Following it to the derelict colony world of Cold Harbor, he finds survivors' descendants living in sealed habitats, erased from every Earth archive because acknowledging them would invalidate the treaty that ended the Frontier Wars. As Earth's final transmission loop counts down to permanent silence, Petra must choose between the woman who saved his life and the duty of exposing a truth that could reignite interstellar war. He broadcasts the massacre records in the loop's last seconds, sacrificing his anonymity and his ship, but winning the colonists their existence—and discovering that belonging was never something he could hide from.
about_author: Marguerite Sandoval is a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Atlantic coast, where she collects dead languages and obsolete radio equipment.

chapters.title: Dead Frequency
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Hauling freight through contested orbits, Petra logs a distress signal in a language he half-remembers from his investigator days—Vessic, extinct for two centuries. His AI insists it's a ghost echo. Curiosity overrides twelve years of practiced invisibility, and he alters course. Beat: restless loneliness cracked open by an impossible sound.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter in Petra's POV, recalling his last case as an insurance investigator: a colony 'lost to reactor failure' whose payout paperwork never added up. He burned the file and quit. Now the signal echoes that old wrongness. Beat: guilt resurfacing; the past refusing to stay filed away.

chapters.title: Cold Harbor
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He reaches a planet marked uninhabited in every chart and finds functioning habitat domes beneath the ice. Before he can decide whether to land, his ship is seized by magnetic tethers. Beat: dread and wonder—the map was a lie, and so is everything built on it.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Speaks to Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ilse Vann's POV. A linguist-archivist among the hidden colonists, Ilse has kept Vessic alive through generations of forbidden teaching. She interrogates the intruder and recognizes his half-buried fluency. Beat: wary fascination—she has waited her whole life for someone outside the ice.

chapters.title: Terms of Salvage
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The colonists' council debates killing him versus keeping him. Ilse argues for trust; the security chief, Doss, argues for the airlock. Petra buys his life by offering what he knows: how Earth's archives are structured, where records hide. Beat: bargaining for breath, dignity traded for utility.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She shows Petra the under-ice memorial: mass graves from the Meridian Massacre, preserved in permafrost, unmarked on any survey. Two hundred thousand people who officially never existed. Beat: grief made physical; horror at how cleanly history was amputated.

chapters.title: The Treaty Clause
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He reconstructs the legal mechanism: the Armistice required 'no surviving belligerent settlements,' so Earth's insurers wrote the colony out of existence rather than void the peace. Proving the massacre means proving the treaty fraudulent. Beat: cold clarity—he understands exactly why they were erased, and by whom.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. She and Petra grow close over translation work, and she learns why he vanished into cargo runs: he testified once, years ago, and a man died for it. Beat: tenderness entangled with recognition—two people who both chose silence to survive.

chapters.title: The Loop
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He calculates Earth's last scheduled transmission loop: nineteen days until the relay network goes permanently dark, after which no broadcast from Cold Harbor can ever reach human space again. A deadline becomes the novel's clock. Beat: urgency crystallizing; the window is closing.

chapters.title: Doss's War
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. The security chief, born after the erasure, believes exposure means bombardment—not vindication. He begins sabotaging Petra's transmitter plans and quietly turns the council. Beat: sympathetic antagonist; fear wearing the mask of loyalty.

chapters.title: Archive Ghosts
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Using his investigator's methods, he locates the original massacre telemetry cached in a decommissioned insurer's relay—a chain of custody he can prove. But retrieving it requires transmitting toward Earth, which Doss will never allow. Beat: triumph shadowed by impossibility; proof without a voice.

chapters.title: First Frost Between Us
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse discovers Petra drafted a plan that uses the colony's power grid as his transmission antenna—draining the domes' life support reserves during broadcast. Love and duty collide inside her. Beat: heartbreak of realizing the man she loves may spend the colony to buy its truth.

chapters.title: Council of the Erased
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, council-chamber scene. Petra presents the evidence and the plan; the colonists confront the choice their grandparents never got: remain safely fictional or risk everything to be real. Vote splits. Beat: democracy under existential pressure; hope and terror sharing a table.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Doss's faction cripples the antenna array and seals the archive vault. Petra is confined, his ship impounded. Ilse refuses to visit him, unable to forgive either plan. Beat: betrayal and isolation; the mission buried under ice twice over.

chapters.title: The Confession Tape
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse finds Doss's private recordings: he has known about the massacre evidence for years and hid it, believing ignorance was the colony's armor. Confronting him, she realizes his loyalty is love, misdirected. Beat: compassion for the enemy; truth as a burden even liars carry.

chapters.title: Nineteen Hours
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Released by a council riven but decided, the colony commits to the broadcast with hours left on the loop. Doss surrenders the vault keys rather than let his people die divided. Beat: reluctant unity; the cost of the choice accepted by all.

chapters.title: Uplink
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Petra's POV. The broadcast drains the domes; frost creeps across nursery windows as the antenna fires the massacre telemetry, the Vessic testimony, and the colonists' own voices toward a dying relay. Beat: sacrifice in real time—warmth traded for witness.

chapters.title: The Last Word
chapters.summary: Climax. Ilse's POV. With seconds remaining, the loop stutters—Earth's automated systems begin quarantining the transmission as hostile. Ilse seizes the mic and speaks in pure Vessic, the language itself proving the speakers exist. The loop accepts and relays before dying forever. Beat: a language rising from extinction to save its children.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Power restored, casualties counted, the colony waits in silence for an answer that may take years—or come as missiles. Doss stands his watch beside Petra, enemies no longer. Beat: exhausted stillness; having spoken, there is nothing to do but endure.

chapters.title: What Comes Back
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Months later, a single reply arrives—not from Earth's government but from scattered listeners, ships, and colonies who received the relay: acknowledgment, solidarity, and one insurer's quiet admission of the fraud. Beat: vindication arriving sideways, imperfect and real.

chapters.title: Named on the Chart
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. New surveys rename Cold Harbor; trade ships request docking codes. Petra, his anonymity gone, chooses to stay rather than vanish again, registering himself in the colony ledger he once investigated from outside. Beat: belonging chosen openly at last; the invisible man signs his name.

chapters.title: The Living Language
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing chapter. At the under-ice memorial, the colonists hold their first public ceremony in two centuries, speaking Vessic aloud. Ilse teaches a class of children; Petra repairs the transmitter, not to warn, but to talk. Beat: resolution—truth survived, love remained, and the extinct language breathes.
